To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HJB equation for infinite horizon control problems with distributed parameters can be solved by a modification of the algorithm originated by González and Rofman, that this algorithm is well suited to be used in the feedback design for distributed parameter systems, and that this algorithm can be successfully combined with POD-based model reduction techniques to solve the HJB equation and to obtain a feedback design for the optimal control of evolution problems.

the combination of model-reduction techniques with the numerical treatment based on the HJB equation of infinite horizon optimal control of PDEs leads to a feasible numerical method for the design of optimal control laws.

the combination of POD with a modified HJB-based numerical algorithm for infinite horizon optimal feedback control of distributed parameter systems leads to significant savings in computational time and storage requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: • the numerical solution of the HJB equation by means of a modified version of a finite difference scheme; • the numerical treatment of a distributed parameter optimal control problem by means of the HJB-POD approach; • the numerical solution for the optimal feedback control law; • the numerical realization of the closed loop optimal control.

, in the case of optimal feedback control of infinite dimensional systems, the combination of model order reduction techniques with HJB-based numerical treatment of the control problem seems to be the most feasible approach.
this work presents a novel methodology to solve the optimal control problem of distributed systems by combining the POD with the numerical solution of the HJB equation.

the combination of the POD-based reduced order models for the state and the HJB-based reduced order models of the value function leads to the efficient computation of the optimal feedback control.
we have developed a methodology for the design of optimal feedback control laws for distributed parameter systems that can be realized in a real-time setting.

a POD-based HJB algorithm for the optimal control of distributed parameter systems is feasible and that the numerical treatment of HJB equations for optimal control of infinite horizon systems is possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of HJB-POD-based feedback control design with model reduction techniques based upon POD is an effective and computationally efficient method for optimal feedback control design of distributed parameter systems.
the combination of the POD and HJB-POD algorithms can be a viable approach for the numerical treatment of infinite horizon optimal control for distributed parameter problems.
the proposed approach is able to achieve a satisfactory tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency in the control design.
